a1.say: Let's build Validated Create Endpoint (201 Created).

a1.cap: Add POST /api/users that accepts {"email": ..., "name": ...}. Reject invalid input with 400 (email must be valid, name 2–50 characters). On success return 201 Created with a Location header pointing to the new user.
a1.say: Add POST /api/users that accepts "email":..., "name":.... Reject invalid input with 400 (email must be valid, name 2 to 50 characters). On success return 201 Created with a Location header pointing to the new user.

a1.cap: Put Bean Validation constraints such as @Email and @Size directly on the request record. Annotating the parameter with @Valid makes Spring validate it before your code runs and answer 400 automatically on failure.
a1.say: Put Bean Validation constraints such as at Email and at Size directly on the request record. Annotating the parameter with at Valid makes Spring validate it before your code runs and answer 400 automatically on failure.

a1.cap: REST convention for creation is 201 with a Location header; ServletUriComponentsBuilder builds that URL from the current request.
a1.say: REST convention for creation is 201 with a Location header; Servlet Uri Components Builder builds that URL from the current request.

a1.cap: The request body is a record with validation rules on each component: a valid, non-blank email and a name of 2 to 50 characters.
A ConcurrentHashMap and an AtomicLong keep this in-memory store safe under concurrent requests.

a1.cap: @RequestBody reads JSON into the record; @Valid runs the constraints and returns 400 Bad Request if any fail.
